wicket.shortText: c Ziaur Rahman b Hashmatullah Shahidi

2124070.postText: Session 1 belonged to Afghanistan thanks to their two centurions, Atal and Rahmanullah. Session 2 belonged to Zimbabwe, courtesy of a collective bowling attack and sharp fielding. Session 3: Well, it is moving day and it finally lived up to that name properly! The major talking point will certainly be Rahmat Shah's catch incident at the slip cordon when he was on 37 runs. Even so, Zimbabwe should be pleased with how they turned things around on a flat pitch and shifted the momentum. Afghanistan finish Day 3 trailing by 102 runs, but Zimbabwe still hold the upper hand in this match in my opinion. We will be back for Day 4 action tomorrow. Until then, take care and see you! 5:17 pm Dropped catches and squandered chances have written a bittersweet story for Zimbabwe in this Test match. This time Alikhil is the lucky one, given a life when Tsiga missed a stumping chance while the batter was on 13. Cremer still got his man eventually though, as Alikhil tried to play square away from his body against the turn, couldn't keep it down, and was caught at cover point by Curran for 40. Rahmat Shah then led the way for Afghanistan as usual, while Qais entertained the viewers with some hefty blows and boundaries. Qais eventually departed, caught behind for 27 off 39 balls, becoming the fourth victim of Nyamhuri's pace. Rahmat Shah remains unbeaten on 94 and will take strike on the morning of Day 4. Hans: "With crossing 400, Afghanistan is going to draw this test match too, especially with Rahmat on the crease. And, if they make it around 450, then the draw is Pakka "guaranteed""

33060.postText: 4.33pm Looks like that's it. The umpires check the light again and it has reached the threshold for this Test. So that's stumps on day 3. But what a historic day for Towhid Hridoy it has been. He was on 29 overnight with Bangladesh 88 for 3. Warrican reduced them to 184 for 7 and it looked like West Indies might take a lead of more than 100. Hridoy had other ideas. He not only shepherded the tail but also kept finding boundaries. Having converted his maiden fifty into a maiden hundred, he went on to breach the 200 mark and break Mushfiqur Rahim's record of 219* for the highest score by a Bangladesh batter. He hit 11 sixes in his innings, another Bangladesh record and just one short of the world record. His effort gave Bangladesh a 30-run lead. Excited Bangladesh, though, then burnt two reviews in the first over of West Indies' second innings. They are still 23 ahead but West Indies have all ten wickets intact. That's all for now. We will be back tomorrow, see you then.
